One spell is linked when the field is created. Whenever stored energy reaches that spell's level, the field automatically casts it at the point chosen when the field was created, expending only the required stored levels; unused levels remain but fade at one level per day. The linked spell uses your level-based effects and duration, and can trigger again after its prior casting ends. Concentration spells cost one stored spell level per hour, and the field's concentration is interrupted only by its destruction. Targeted linked spells choose the nearest living creature. Linked spells cannot have an XP cost or costly material component; costly focuses are allowed only if present in the field. Only Mordenkainen's disjunction, limited wish, wish, or similarly powerful magic can destroy the field; lower-level dispels are absorbed. Antimagic prevents absorption inside its area but otherwise does not end the field. Overlapping transformation fields have an equal chance to absorb an effect used in their overlap.

name: Polymorph Other
effectSummary: On a failed Fortitude save, permanently changes one creature into another creature form from Diminutive size up to one size category larger than the subject's normal form. On changing, the subject recovers lost hit points as though it had rested for a day, but this does not restore temporary ability damage or provide other rest benefits, and changing back does not heal it again; if slain, it reverts to its original form but remains dead. The subject takes the chosen form's average natural size, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, natural armor, natural attack routines and other gross physical qualities, plus mundane movement capabilities such as walking, swimming, or winged flight and other nonmagical natural abilities such as low-light vision. It does not gain magical movement or the new form's spell-like, supernatural, or extraordinary abilities. The subject keeps its Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, level and class, hit points despite any Constitution change, alignment, base attack bonus, base saves, original creature type, its own extraordinary abilities, spells, and spell-like abilities, but not its own supernatural abilities. It can cast spells only when the new form can supply the required components, including a humanlike voice for verbal components and humanlike hands for somatic components. Any separated body part or piece of equipment returns to its original form. In stressful or demanding situations such as combat, the subject must succeed on a DC 19 Will save or take a -2 penalty on attack rolls, saves, skill checks, and ability checks until the situation passes; a creature kept polymorphed for years may overcome some of this disorientation at the DM's discretion. Equipment changes to match the form: for forms that do not use equipment, gear melds into the body and becomes nonfunctional, including material components and focuses; for forms that use equipment, the gear changes to fit and retains its properties, with the chosen creature's entry deciding doubtful cases. You can choose cosmetic and significant physical traits within the normal range for the species, including changing the subject into its own species or itself; changing it into itself avoids the disorientation penalty, and using the spell as a disguise grants a +10 bonus on Disguise checks. Incorporeal or gaseous forms cannot be assumed, incorporeal or gaseous creatures are immune to the spell, and a natural shapeshifter can resume its natural form as a standard action. The material component is an empty cocoon.

name: Summon Living Dragonmark
effectSummary: Summons one neutral Medium ooze-shaped living dragonmark at a point within range for 1 round per level; it acts immediately on your turn, attacks opponents to the best of its ability, can be directed to particular enemies, and cannot perform other actions. You can have only one living dragonmark summoned at a time, and the spell requires a lesser, greater, or Siberys true dragonmark. The creature has initiative +4; blindsight 60 feet; Listen +0 and Spot +0; fly speed 60 feet (perfect); 6 HD; base attack +4; grapple +8; Strength 18, Dexterity 18, Constitution —, Intelligence —, Wisdom 11, Charisma 10; Fortitude +2, Reflex +6, Will +2; damage reduction 10/magic; immunity to acid, cold, electricity, fire, sonic, positive energy, negative energy, and the normal ooze immunities. Its AC includes its +4 Dexterity bonus plus a deflection bonus equal to the summoner's Charisma modifier. A mark summoned by a caster with a lesser dragonmark has 33 hit points; one summoned by a greater or Siberys mark has 48 hit points. Its force slam attack is +8 and deals damage by mark strength: Lesser 1d6+6, Greater 1d8+6, Siberys 2d6+6. On a successful slam it can use improved grab to begin a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity; after establishing a hold it can constrict for normal force-slam damage on a successful grapple check, but cannot constrict a creature larger than itself.

name: Symbol
effectSummary: Scribes one potent rune using either a quick 1-action form or a carefully engraved 10-minute form. A quick rune activates immediately, glows faintly, and lasts 10 minutes per caster level; only fear, hopelessness, pain, or persuasion can be quick. A careful rune remains inactive until triggered, must be visible/prominent, and uses configurable triggers such as reading, touching, passing over/through, looking at it, or special conditions based on name, identity, alignment, or observable qualities, never level/class/HD/hit points; triggering requires being within 60 feet. The caster is immune and can attune creatures/passwords as the source allows. Variants are: Death, killing the closest creatures whose combined current hp fit within a 150-hp total, Fortitude negates; Discord, causing Int 3+ creatures to bicker and potentially fight, Will negates; Fear, a powerful fear effect, Will negates, with careful engraving raising the DC by 4; Hopelessness, Will negates, leaving victims hopeless for 3d4x10 minutes and compliant/withdrawn; Insanity, affecting up to 150 combined hp as Insanity, Will negates; Pain, imposing -2 Dexterity and -4 on attacks, skills, and ability checks for 2d10x10 minutes, Fortitude negates, careful engraving +4 DC; Persuasion, Will negates, changing alignment to the caster's and making the subject friendly as Charm Person for 1d20x10 minutes, careful engraving +4 DC; Sleep, affecting creatures of 8 HD or less with catatonic sleep for 3d6x10 minutes, Will negates; and Stunning, affecting up to 250 combined hp, Fortitude negates, stunning victims so they lose Dexterity to AC, attackers gain +2, and held items drop. Read Magic plus Spellcraft DC 19 identifies a rune, potentially triggering it; targeted Dispel Magic removes it, Erase does not, and destroying the inscribed surface triggers and destroys it. Material components are mercury and phosphorus; careful engraving additionally uses diamond and opal worth at least 5,000 gp each.

name: Symbol of Death
effectSummary: Scribes a visible rune with configurable trigger conditions. When triggered, it becomes a 60-foot burst that attempts to slay the closest creatures whose combined current hit points do not exceed 150; creatures too healthy to fit the remaining total are skipped. Fortitude negates and spell resistance applies. The active rune lasts 10 minutes per caster level or until it has affected 150 hit points of creatures. A creature saves only once while continuously inside, but must save again after leaving and re-entering. Default triggers can include looking at, reading, touching, passing over, or passing through a portal bearing the rune, and no trigger can occur from more than 60 feet away. Special limits can use observable qualities, name, identity, or alignment, but not class, Hit Dice, level, or hit points. A password grants immunity while within 60 feet, and creatures can be attuned during casting; the caster is automatically attuned. Read magic plus Spellcraft DC 19 identifies it, potentially triggering a read-triggered rune. A targeted dispel magic can remove it; erase cannot; destroying the inscribed surface destroys and triggers it. Permanency can make it permanent, in which case a disabled or exhausted rune resets after 10 minutes. A rogue can find and disable it at DC 33. Material components are mercury and phosphorus plus powdered diamond and opal at the source-listed value of at least 5,000 gp each.
